brief: The FOMC unanimously (12-0, versus 9-3 in July) raised its target rate range 25bps to 3.75%-4% and guided at least one more hike by year-end with high conviction; a large but non-majority contingent sees a further hike in 2027. The median dot points to a total 50bps of hikes this year with adjustments done by year-end; the mode extends to 75bps by 2027. Sixteen of eighteen members expect another hike, four expect three total this year. Markets read the move as hawkish: 2yr yields +14bps, 10yr +8bps in a bear flattener, the dollar firmed against all majors, the S&P500 fell about 3/4%, and OIS now prices 100bps of total tightening. The SEP raised 2026 growth to 2.3% and lifted near-term PCE and core PCE inflation, while cutting the unemployment path to 4.1%. The statement dropped its supply-shock inflation language and upgraded demand-side wording. Scotiabank's Derek Holt argues this risks policy error, since growth risks skew lower and feedback effects may exceed the Committee's expectations. He also expects the hike gives the Bank of Canada, which meets in October, more cover to hike, leaving the Bank of England as the only other major holdout.
